question: At the end of September, the European Commission published a positive audit report on the Brazilian control system for certain antimicrobial substances in the poultry and honey sectors. This paved the way for the lifting of import restrictions. In Brazilian beef production, however, problems persisted regarding the use of, and controls on, 17β-oestradiol, a hormone that is banned for this purpose in the EU.1 1.
What additional checks will be carried out following the positive audit in September 2026 to ensure that Brazilian poultry producers continue to comply with EU rules and regulations?
How many consignments of Brazilian poultry meat and beef have been rejected in the past three years due to breaches of EU food safety or residue standards?
How does the Commission ensure that imported animal products comply with the applicable EU health requirements?
